parent_review.original_I139_audit: I142 independently passes original A139 and B139 without repairs at their stated scopes. It retains the eta-dependent entrance, simultaneous finite minors, fixed original graded saturation, common very-general locus, real/boundary nef limits, arbitrary given nef bubble inputs, algebraic normal-cone family and finite refinements. Original I133 literal I.5 remains FAIL separately from its finite-initial-norm correction. Parent checks here are selective, not an independent second full original audit.
selected_mathematical_checks: For each geometric weight bin, u_l^(n-1) sum w_i is at most (1+epsilon)^(n-1) sum w_i^n. A completed greedy group wastes less than u_l^n relative to h_l^n. Rounding its group count to a multiple of n! costs at most n! h_l^n beyond A_l/(1-K^(-n)). Summing the geometric h_l^n bound pays all possible levels independently of the smallest weight or number of occupied bins.

The common grid scale is H=KM and each h_l is dyadic relative to H. Processing cube requests in decreasing size leaves free cubes no smaller than the next request, with volumes integer multiples of that size. The total capacity inequality therefore gives an actual finite placement, not merely a scalar packing heuristic.

Every point of 2H*1+(1-4H c_P)P has coordinates at least 2H and weighted sum at most 1-2H c_P. A containing closed H-grid cube has strictly positive coordinates and weighted sum at most 1-H c_P. Hence its closure is interior. Bernoulli gives the stated available-capacity bound, with the additional factor-eight margin safe.

Strict U permits a fixed small zeta in the greedy cutoff. The resulting group envelopes are strictly below their cell capacities, and K>=400 leaves room for contraction while keeping the local /100 entrance. For the fixed finite vector, all local supports can remain in fixed compact cell interiors; rounding degree-scaled translations costs only bounded exponents.

The cumulative-column simplex maps are integral unimodular. The sum of absolute coordinate differences is convex with unique affine maximizing pieces on the strict permutation chambers. The stated normalized finite matrix has a block-diagonal limit. Higher dyadic and top-grid nodes then use strict coordinate cuts and previously obtained simultaneous minors, choosing parent parameters after child parameters. This is finite induction, not an assumption of global coherence for a hanging-node triangulation.

Original full-density graded saturation applies once the assembled selected columns lie in one fixed compact subset of the original flag simplex. The assembled degreewise support union itself need not be graded. Finite rank transfer and countably many degree conditions give a very-general tuple; rational strict parameters and weights on a common locus precede real nef limits. Exact volume-boundary jet surjectivity is not asserted.

With K=M^(-1/(n+1)) and epsilon=M^(n/(n+1)), both F-1 and the boundary loss are O(M^(n/(n+1))), and the rounding loss is O(M^(n(n-1)/(n+1))). For n>=3 this proves the stated sufficient shrinking-volume error. For a fixed positive vector, however, M does not tend to zero and U has a positive loss at Q=V. It cannot be closed to the exact boundary with an unchanged entrance.

The continuous bubble construction uses eta=1/4 on Pn and q chosen so that its largest child is below 1/1600 uniformly in t. Its two equal blocks have exact capacities t and 1-t. Actual A139 nef inputs feed the arbitrary-input B139 operation at each equal root. Independent real parameters and finite refinements give multi-level nonreciprocal boundary vectors, with countable rational approximation before real limits.

The grammar G is explicitly restricted to equal/power, one-envelope and two-envelope primitives. At full volume the envelope defect is zero, forcing equality within each positive block. Entrance bounds rule out a full-volume unary or binary envelope node. Every nonidentity edge has capacity factor at most one half; equal unary contractions retain their lost capacity when suppressed.

For a fixed positive full-volume target with minimum mu, a retained path has parent capacity at least (mu/2)^n, so its nonidentity depth is bounded logarithmically. The finite union of r paths has boundedly many nodes. The nonnegative telescoping capacity losses force relevant seed deficits and omitted-child capacities to vanish. After a subsequence, the pruned finite boundary tree still has a deepest nontrivial node with repeated terminal weights. This excludes pairwise-distinct fixed positive targets from the tree closure, even with unbounded discarded branches.

For a positive l_n boundary vector, its supporting functional has a strict gap away from any neighborhood of that vector. Convex combinations approaching the boundary target therefore require underlying generated vectors approaching it. Internal convex combinations expand by multilinearity of finite refinements; downward and deletion operations and fixed-length limits can be approximated before finite continuous operations. Thus the stated obstruction covers the defined combined grammar, not arbitrary nef inputs or U142.

The profile p_i=2i/[r(r+1)] has distinct positive coordinates, total normalized volume one and maximum tending to zero. Its exclusion from G supplies no negative-intersection curve and is not a counterexample to W136. Neither the strict-slack route nor the continuous bubble route proves or refutes that conjecture.
